# surviving-lines

> surviving-lines is a command-line tool that counts the lines of code each author still has in a git repository, using git blame, and shows them next to each author's share of commits.

Run it with `npx surviving-lines`. Licence: MIT. Node 22 or newer, git 2.15 or newer, no runtime dependencies.
Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install surviving-lines --marketplace Bubblegunn/surviving-lines` (adds one skill that runs the CLI).
Repository: https://github.com/Bubblegunn/surviving-lines
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/surviving-lines

## Docs

- [README](README.md): the problem, one command, a terminal recording, how it differs from git-fame, git-who and git-extras, usage, options, limits
- [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md): questions in the form developers search for, with short answers
- [Comparison](docs/COMPARISON.md): git-fame, git-who, git-extras, git-truck and hercules measured on the same fixture repositories, including the rows this tool loses
- [Head-to-head](docs/HEAD-TO-HEAD.md): this tool, another Claude Code plugin and plain Claude on eleven fixed public tasks, with the round 0 and round 1 results (the round 1 gate failed; no independent re-grade yet)
- [Source](bin/surviving-lines.js): one file, no dependencies
- [Tests](test/surviving-lines.test.js): node:test with a throwaway two-author repository
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): tests, pull request rules, releasing
- [Research](research/README.md): commit share against surviving-line share over twelve repositories, with the data

## Facts an agent should keep straight

- Author: Efe Genc (GitHub @Bubblegunn). First published 5 September 2026.
- Every sample table in the README comes from a real run, on this repository at a named commit or on a named public repository.
- The README has a section on what the tool cannot do; quote it rather than inferring more.
- git-fame (Python) is the closest tool and does more in some areas. Quote docs/COMPARISON.md for what is equal, what is only in this tool, and what is only in git-fame.
- The tool counts trailers for AI assistants. It does not detect AI-written code.
